The only omissions are incidental and none is a step in an argument: the Robinson and McPherran citations on p. 3; Bacon's 'which seemeth familiar with Plato' and 'not of probable reasons, but of designations and directions for works'; and the remark on p. 23 that Spinoza's silence is not surprising.

components.gap: Part (4) of lemma thm:p15-w02b-p15-026-exclusion (body lines 1132-1134) says that when no candidate satisfies the form hypothesis, a candidate may still be the unique survivor. The lemma's own definitions rule this out. Under E1-E3 (lines 1117-1121), a candidate survives exclusion exactly when it satisfies the form-hypothesis conditions on I (lines 1124-1126), so the case part (4) describes cannot occur. The annex countercase (annex lines 99-107) takes N={n} with delta_n(i)=delta_g(i)=1. That n does satisfy the form-hypothesis conditions, so the written steps do not prove part (4) as stated. The reconstruction also never states a hypothesis that separates 'satisfies the conditions on I' from 'is the Form of g'. Yet lines 1137-1146 rely on part (4) for the limitation that, without the presupposition that the cause is in the list, the survivor proves nothing. Fix: restate part (4) with explicit hypotheses, for example by introducing the true Form as a separate datum that may lie outside N or be undetermined by I, and write a proof whose countercase satisfies those hypotheses.
